notes.note: Enchanted dishes walking about on their own: my kind of kitchen. Eight or sixteen directions, one per way a line can run, is a hut turning round to find its door.
Smart enough. Taste written down as rules is a mortar with the recipe carved into its side: useful, and only a little dangerous, which is how I like my magic.
I disagree a little. Guardians should not keep their own ledger; a witch who marks her own homework comes out top every time. Let someone outside the panel count.
Two families of guardians, Claude and Codex: a witch trusts neither entirely, which is how a panel stays honest. The Mac on Kubernetes? A hut on a server rack. But alas.
Witchy, yes. Halloween-store witchy, no. Keep the pointed hats and owls on the shelf. Medea would bring a mortar, a broom and a little temper, which is a far better outfit.
Codex built the engine, and it renders the same to the byte every run. There is my wink: a tool doing the work by itself, and not a broom in sight.

favorite_idea.why: A coloring book that keeps its stories in the margins is the ink and ornamental border I would frame, because a margin is where a guardian gets to scribble.

steer: Keep the footnotes few and sharp, and let Paul's own words carry the magic, since a charm works best when it is short.
